newsitem.title: JAMAICA: SHAREHOLDERS OF JAMAICAN BREWER APPROVE NEW STOCK.
newsitem.headline: SHAREHOLDERS OF JAMAICAN BREWER APPROVE NEW STOCK.

text.p: Shareholders of Desnoes & Geddes, brewers of Red Stripe beer, have approved a $25.7 million rights issue to raise capital as part of a five-year expansion program, the company said Wednesday.
The rights issue, an issue of new stock to existing shareholders, was approved Tuesday, the company said.
D&G, traded on the Kingston stock exchange, is majority owned by Guinness Plc . The largest minority shareholders are Heineken NV and members of the Desnoes and Geddes families.
Guinness agreed to underwrite the rights issues, part of $714 million the brewer will invest in the Jamaican company over five years.

D&G has gone through a rough period since Guinness acquired control several years ago. It controls some 90 percent of the local beer and stout market, but sales have slumped as inflation pushed up prices.

The brewery also once controlled 90 percent of soft drink sales, but cheaper drinks produced by a rival firm, as well as imports from Trinidad and Canada, have cut deeply into D&G's market share over the past year.
Guinness was looking to broaden the export market for the flagship product, Red Stripe.
The company was heartened by recent press reports that U.S. President Bill Clinton ordered Red Stripe during a dinner with British Prime Minister Tony Blair during his recent visit to Europe.
